correctness.rationale: For 0<xi0<1 and off-origin relocation one, the exact two-state origin conditional probability leads to a bounded supermartingale forcing origin frequency to zero. The log-count martingale gives C_n=n^(1-o(1)) almost surely; reciprocal-fraction errors and martingale quadratic variations are then summable. Harmonic telescoping proves Q_n-p log C_n converges to a finite random limit and hence gives a sharp -p loglog n correction. Every core algebra identity was checked with exact rationals across 27224 state-parameter combinations and the finite-state distribution recursion was checked on 1521 reachable transitions; computations supplement the proof.

originality.rationale: The exact-endpoint pathwise reciprocal origin count with dimension-independent coefficient, harmonic constant, and negative loglog term was compared against the current impurity-walk theorem and the strongest earlier stationarity calculation. Boyer et al. already claim the qualitative neighbor-supported limit as q tends to one: that fact is deliberately not claimed as new. Neither inspected mathematical statement implies the quantitative almost-sure expansion at q=1. Published semantic records and broad primary-literature searches yielded no direct coverage; priority remains qualified by a potential general reinforcement theorem.
residual_risks: A general theorem for random-copying processes with a state-dependent mutation at an impurity might implicitly subsume the count expansion.
The 2019 stationary self-consistency treatment anticipates the qualitative endpoint-support picture; no novelty is assigned to this qualitative prediction.
Semantic research-record search is non-exhaustive and no independent priority review has been performed.

value.rationale: At the singular perfect-relocation boundary of a physically motivated non-Markovian walk, the qualitative concentration profile leaves the finite-time frequency of the impurity unresolved. The result quantifies that frequency with a dimension-free leading constant and a universal logarithm-of-logarithm correction; the stronger pathwise renormalized finite-limit statement separates it from the previously predicted q-to-one stationary profile.
